item.title: Elder Rāhula: Blinded by sensual desires, Covered by the net of wrong views, Craving acts as a veil, Covering, hiding completely. Bound by heedlessness, Like…
item.description:
Elder Rāhula:

Blinded by sensual desires,
Covered by the net of wrong views,
Craving acts as a veil,
Covering, hiding completely.
Bound by heedlessness,
Like a fish caught in a net.

I have overcome those sensual desires,
Cut Māra’s bondage.
Having pulled out the root of craving,
I am cooled, at peace.

From: Theragāthā 4.8

item.title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is an establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: "When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the…
item.description:
"When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — that cause the monk restrains, guards the eye faculty... By means of this noble restraint of the faculties, he experiences an internal feeling of ease, unblemished."

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: “Fletchers make arrows, Potters make pots, Carpenters shape wood, The wise tame themselves.” “Like a solid rock Unmoved by the wind, So the wise are…
item.description:
“Fletchers make arrows,
Potters make pots,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.”

“Like a solid rock
Unmoved by the wind,
So the wise are unmoved
Amid praise and blame.”

“Like a deep lake,
Clear, unruffled,
So the wise become serene,
Hearing the Dhamma.”

“The good renounce everything,
The virtuous do not prattle about sensual desires.
Whether touched by pleasure or pain,
The wise show neither elation nor depression.”

From: Dhammapada 76-89
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely…
item.description:
“Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. Thus, monks, a monk does not know forms. Monks, how is a monk one who is not skillful in characteristics? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is the fool and the characteristics of a fool, the wise person and the characteristics of a wise person. Thus, monks, a monk is not skillful in characteristics. Monks, how is a monk one who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly? Here, monks, a monk indulges in arisen sensual thoughts; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. He indulges in arisen ill-will thoughts … harmful thoughts … evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 33 – Mahāgopālakasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Abandon desire, abandon greed — These are the bonds of worldlings. The one with eyes walks the path, Crosses hell and human birth. Eating little,…
item.description:
“Abandon desire, abandon greed —
These are the bonds of worldlings.
The one with eyes walks the path,
Crosses hell and human birth.

Eating little, moderate in food,
With few wishes, not greedy —
He is without desire, without craving,
Truly at peace.

Having gone on alms-round,
The sage enters the forest,
Goes to the root of a tree,
Prepares his sitting place.

The wise one, meditating,
Delights in the forest,
Meditating at the root of a tree,
Content, he practices his own pleasure.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.11
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who…
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who attends unwisely, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.66
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by…
item.description:
Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by sensual pleasures. Then the Blessed One, understanding the meaning, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

Blinded by sensual pleasures,
Covered by a net,
Veiled by craving,
Bound by the fetter of heedlessness —
Like fish caught in a net,
They go to aging and death,
Like a suckling calf to its mother.

From: Udana 7.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises…
item.description:
“So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there. The ear is not the bondage of sounds … The nose is not the bondage of odors … The tongue is not the bondage of tastes … The body is not the bondage of touches … The mind is not the bondage of phenomena, nor are phenomena the bondage of the mind. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 41.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior fights with noble warrior, brahmin fights with brahmin, householder fights with householder, mother fights with child, child fights with mother, father fights with child, child fights with father, brother fights with brother, brother fights with sister, sister fights with brother, friend fights with friend. Having engaged in quarrels, disputes, and battles, they attack one another with fists, with stones, with sticks, with swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta
